title: Publish your first draft BRD
why_matters: Week 6 is the bend in the curve. You've been listening, mapping, asking. Now you need a piece of work that survives contact with stakeholders. A BRD is the cleanest test: it's structured enough to defend, public enough to provoke reaction, durable enough to hand to engineering.
steps: Pick a piece of in-scope work you have enough context to scope. Don't pick the biggest; pick the smallest that's worth doing right.
Use the BRD-standard playbook. Write through every section, including out-of-scope. Aim for two pages, not eight.
Get one critical pre-read — your line manager or a senior BA. Take their notes; don't dismiss any.
Publish. Send it to the stakeholders on your map, with a one-line explanation of what you'd like feedback on by when.
success_criteria: A two-page BRD is published. Three or more stakeholders have received it with a specific feedback ask and a deadline. Manager has pre-read and acknowledged.
reflection_prompt: Which section did you most want to leave vague, and what did the discipline of filling it in reveal?
